Customer: Mike H: hey team :wave: we've got a crash report from a handful of customers — after they re-enroll MFA the web session immediately drops and they end up back at the login screen. Happens in Chrome mobile and in-app webviews.

Alice K (support): thanks Mike — can you paste an example user id / account id and whether this is hosted or private? any recent config changes? :thinking_face:

Customer: Mike H: account 12345, user mike.h@example.com. Hosted. No config changes on their side; they re-enrolled from settings -> Security. In devtools we see a Set-Cookie for `refresh_token` sent by re-enroll handler, then immediately another Set-Cookie with `Max-Age=0` that clears the cookie. The sequence looks like: re-enroll -> POST /auth/mfa/re-enroll -> 302 redirect -> on redirect cookie cleared. Logs show `device_jwt: invalid_signature` for the subsequent request.

Alice K (support): OK copying to eng. Jordan, Maya — can you take a look? I'll keep the customer posted.

Jordan S (eng): looking. can you reproable with a curl flow? also what domain/path are cookies set on? might be a path mismatch.

Customer: Mike H: here's a quick curl I used to simulate re-enroll:

```bash
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/auth/mfa/re-enroll \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <SESSION_JWT>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"method":"otp","device_name":"pixel-6"}'
```

Response headers from the above:

```
HTTP/1.1 302 Found
Set-Cookie: refresh_token=eyJ...; Path=/auth; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict; Max-Age=2592000
Set-Cookie: refresh_token=; Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=None; Max-Age=0
Location: /app
```

Jordan S (eng): that header sequence is the smoking gun. First cookie set with `Path=/auth` then a clear for `Path=/`. Browsers treat those separately; the clear for `/` will remove the more specific cookie in some clients (and webviews). We have code that clears stale refresh cookies on session rekey — looks like it runs in a middleware that assumes the new cookie will be issued on the same `Path` as the old one. If the re-enroll handler issues `Path=/auth` and the global clear uses `/` we end up clearing the freshly minted cookie.

Maya (sre): reproduction confirmed on Chrome Android webview. Also seen in our logs: the `clear_cookie()` call is invoked on the post-rekey path because the old device_jwt validation fails (we rotate device_jwt during re-enroll) and the middleware treats that as a potential hijack and clears all refresh cookies using `Path=/`.

Ryan (oncall): workaround for customers: ask them to open the re-enroll flow in full browser (not embedded webview) — webview cookie handling differs for cross-path clears. But we need a real fix.

Jordan S (eng): proposed fix: ensure the re-enroll endpoint sets cookie path to `/` (same as clear) OR make the clear routine only target the specific path used when the cookie was set. Safer: preserve the `Path`/`SameSite` attributes of the incoming refresh cookie when rotating. I'll open a PR to normalize path handling in the rekey flow.

Alice K (support): do we have a quick mitigation we can apply for the affected tenant while PR is reviewed?

Jordan S (eng): yes — feature flag `ALLOW_REENROLL_COOKIE_PATH_MISMATCH=true` to temporarily disable the aggressive clear during rekey on non-enterprise tenants. Turning it on avoids clearing newly issued cookies. I'll coordinate with ops.

Maya (sre): turned the flag on for account 12345 at 14:12 UTC. Customer reports immediate improvement — users stay signed in after re-enroll. We'll keep it on until the patch deploy.

Jordan S (eng): root cause summary I'll add to the ticket: re-enroll flow issued refresh cookie with `Path=/auth` while cookie-clear middleware used `Path=/` to clear. Race: rotate -> issue new cookie (narrow path) -> generic clear removes cookie. Fix is to align path semantics and preserve cookie attributes on rotate.

Jordan S (eng): repro steps I used locally:

1) Login with session and refresh cookie set on `/`
2) Simulate re-enroll handler that sets cookie with `Path=/auth`
3) Trigger rekey middleware that runs `clear_all_refresh_cookies(path='/')`
4) Observe that browser treats set+clear as clearing final cookie causing next request to fail auth

Example code snippet showing the vulnerable call: 

```python
# pseudo
def rotate_refresh_cookie(resp, new_token):
    resp.set_cookie('refresh_token', new_token, path='/auth', httponly=True, secure=True)

# middleware
if not device_jwt_valid:
    clear_all_refresh_cookies(path='/')  # too broad
```

Jordan S (eng): PR: https://git.internal.redwood/eng/pulls/4723 — normalizes cookie path to `/` for all refresh cookie rotations and updates clear routine to accept specific path(s). Also adds tests that simulate webview behavior.

Alice K (support): great. ETA on deployment?

Maya (sre): will stage deploy in ~30m, manual QA on mobile webview then prod deploy after 1h if green.

SupportBot: deploy-bot: starting deployment of eng/pulls/4723 to staging (build 9012).. :gear:

Ryan (oncall): staging looks good on my check. re-enroll flow stays signed in on Chrome Android webview.

SupportBot: deploy-bot: succeeded deploy eng/pulls/4723 to staging (build 9012) :white_check_mark:

Maya (sre): rolling to prod in 20m. will keep flag enabled for 1h post-deploy and then disable if no regressions.

SupportBot: deploy-bot: promoted eng/pulls/4723 to prod (build 9012) :rocket:

Alice K (support): customer updated: "seems fixed, users can re-enroll and remain signed in" :) I'll mark this resolved for account 12345 and follow up after flag removal.

Customer: Mike H: thank you all — appreciate the quick turnaround :pray:

Jordan S (eng): adding postmortem note to the ticket: impact=medium, root_cause=cookie-path-rotation-mismatch, mitigation=feature-flag + path normalization PR, followup=add e2e webview tests and audit cookie attribute handling.

Maya (sre): logging action item: run a scan for any endpoints that set refresh cookie with non-root paths. I'll assign to eng-infra for a sweep.

Alice K (support): closing loop with customer later today.
